claims.text: The local catalog models the World Challenge Secret Super Battle Best in Japan second-place prize source group as one row containing No.2 Trainer at source index 200.
Bulbapedia says No.2 Trainer began as a Japanese tournament Trainer card and later became a prize in the Pokémon World Championships.

Bulbapedia says top-ranking players from Secret Super Battle were eligible to compete in a Best in Japan Deciding Match in late August 2000, while overall winners of Tropical Mega Battle regional events represented Japan in the World Exchange Battle in Hawaii.
Pokumon places the Secret Super Battle Best in Japan Deciding Match at Pokémon Center Tokyo in Tokyo, Japan on August 19, 2000.
Bulbapedia says runners-up of the Best in Japan finals were awarded Holofoil No.2 Trainer cards bearing their photograph superimposed on the illustration.

Pokumon reports that winners of the Secret Super Battle Best in Japan event received No.1-3 Trainer trophy cards, that each is reported to be cosmos holofoil with the winner's photograph printed onto it, and that no photos have surfaced to confirm that report.
Bulbapedia says the World Challenge Summer No.2 Trainer major iteration used new artwork by Ken Sugimori.

Bulbapedia describes Ken Sugimori as a friend of Satoshi Tajiri, illustrator of the original Pokémon game artwork, illustrator of TCG cards and merchandise, and the artist who redrew all 151 Generation I Pokémon in watercolor for promotional use.

Pokumon says World Challenge Summer 2000 separated Tropical Mega Battle for players aged 14 or under from Secret Super Battle for players 15+, supporting the senior-track boundary for this Best in Japan route.

This second-place Best in Japan card must be separated from regional Secret Super Battle No.2 Trainer cards, which Bulbapedia describes as Non Holofoil, personalized with winner name and regional conference, and based on male/female Trainer versions.

Agents must identify this as the World Challenge Secret Super Battle Best in Japan second-place route before using No.2 Trainer value, rarity, or lore. The special rail must preserve final-stage senior-track context, Holofoil/photo-trophy signals, and boundaries against regional SSB, TMB/Hawaii, Worlds, Challenge Road, Lizardon/Kamex, Neo Road, Battle Road, and name-only No.2 Trainer claims.

As judged collector texture, the Secret Super Battle Best in Japan No.2 Trainer matters because it turns the final domestic senior runner-up into a card-object: rank, route, venue, trophy lineage, and reportedly the player's photograph all compressed into a single unnumbered promo.
not_claiming: that reported photograph details are enough to identify a specific seller card

narrative.human_title: No.2 Trainer [SSB Best in Japan]: the runner-up made photographic
narrative.why_it_matters: Second place has a different charge than first. It carries the ache of almost, but here the almost was still rare enough to be made into a trophy card. This is not the regional non-holo SSB prize and not the junior Tropical Mega Battle path to Hawaii; it is the senior Best in Japan final at Pokemon Center Tokyo. Bulbapedia gives the Holofoil photograph-superimposed story for No.2 Trainer; Pokumon adds the more fragile collector note that the SSB Best in Japan cards are reported as cosmos photo trophies, while no photos have surfaced to confirm the report. The rank is part of the identification, and the identification is the story.
not_claiming: that every No.2 Trainer listing uses this same route
that reported photo-trophy details alone authenticate a listing

special_identification_instructions.trigger: Use when a card, listing, slab label, auction description, or agent claim says No.2 Trainer, World Challenge, Secret Super Battle, Best in Japan, second place, runner-up, senior division, 15+, Pokemon Center Tokyo, Holofoil, cosmos, winner photograph, printed photo, superimposed photo, Tropical Mega Battle, Hawaii, or World Exchange Battle.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Treat No.2 Trainer as a reusable trophy-card title. Establish the Secret Super Battle Best in Japan second-place route before comparing value, rarity, or historical meaning.
steps: Confirm the card is No.2 Trainer / Ｎｏ.２トレーナー and that the claimed promotion is World Challenge Secret Super Battle Best in Japan second-place prize, not regional Secret Super Battle, Tropical Mega Battle, Challenge Road '99, Lizardon Mega Battle, Kamex Mega Battle, Neo Road, Battle Road, World Championships, or name-only No.2 Trainer.
Preserve the senior-track split: Pokumon describes Secret Super Battle as the 15+ track and Tropical Mega Battle as the 14-or-under track.
Preserve the finals venue and date as a source-backed route clue: Pokumon places Secret Super Battle Best in Japan at Pokemon Center Tokyo on August 19, 2000.

Separate this final-stage card from regional Secret Super Battle No.2 Trainer cards. Regional SSB cards are described as Non Holofoil, personalized with winner name and regional conference, and route to the Best in Japan machinery rather than being the Best in Japan second-place card itself.

Treat Holofoil, cosmos holofoil, winner photograph, superimposed photograph, and printed photograph as important route clues, but not as authentication. Bulbapedia and Pokumon differ in detail and Pokumon notes that no photos have surfaced to confirm the reported SSB finals photo cards.

Do not treat the Hawaii / World Exchange Battle story as this card's route. Bulbapedia assigns the Hawaii representative path to Tropical Mega Battle regional winners, not Secret Super Battle Best in Japan.

Before spending or trade gating, require seller-controlled photos of the actual card, including full front/back, Holofoil/photo area, any name or rank text, edges, surface, and slab label if graded; catalog identity is legible support, not physical truth.
not_claiming: that No.2 Trainer name alone identifies the exact print
that Holofoil or photo claims alone authenticate the card
that a grading label alone resolves the route

claims.text: The local catalog row identifies source index 200 as No.2 Trainer from the World Challenge Secret Super Battle Best in Japan second-place prize slice.
Bulbapedia gives the Japanese name as Ｎｏ.２トレーナー and describes No.2 Trainer as a Japanese tournament Trainer/Item card lineage used for second-place or runner-up prizes.
Bulbapedia says runners-up of the Best in Japan finals were awarded Holofoil No.2 Trainer cards bearing their photograph superimposed on the illustration.

Pokumon identifies this No.2 Trainer as a World Challenge Secret Super Battle Best in Japan 2000 Japanese unnumbered Trainer Winner card illustrated by Ken Sugimori, with cosmos holofoil treatment and an estimated copy count of one; this dossier treats the copy count as a collector estimate, not official disclosure.
Bulbapedia says the World Challenge Summer No.2 Trainer major iteration used new artwork by Ken Sugimori; Pokumon also labels this Best in Japan No.2 Trainer card with Ken Sugimori.

As interpretive art context, Sugimori's credit matters because a final-stage tournament runner-up card borrows the franchise's original visual authority while turning a real player result into a collectible object.

This card must be separated from World Challenge Secret Super Battle regional No.2 Trainer, World Challenge Tropical Mega Battle No.2 Trainer, World Exchange Battle/Hawaii route cards, Challenge Road '99, Lizardon Mega Battle, Kamex Mega Battle, Neo Road, Battle Road, World Championships No.2 Trainer, and name-only No.2 Trainer listings.

As judged collector texture, No.2 Trainer [World Challenge Secret Super Battle Best in Japan second place] is the senior final runner-up becoming a card: the rank is printed, the route is legible, and the reported photo treatment makes the human result difficult to separate from the object.

narrative.human_title: No.2 Trainer: the final senior runner-up inside the card
narrative.why_it_matters: No.2 Trainer is beautiful because it refuses the easy collector habit of only caring about first place. In this route, second place still reached the senior Best in Japan final, still got fixed into a Holofoil/photo-trophy story, and still needs the exact assembly read before the card can be understood. The object is not just a rank. It is a trace of how early organized play honored the whole shape of a final table.
not_claiming: that every No.2 Trainer print follows this route
that catalog identity makes evidence spendable
